questions.q: How is this ticket's symptom different in cause from Lesson 8's 'payment missing from GL' ticket, even though both start as 'Accounted – Final but not in GL'?
options: They are exactly the same cause
This ticket is caused by a closed period
Lesson 8 was a timing gap fixed by running Transfer to GL; this ticket persisted even after Transfer to GL ran successfully twice, pointing to a different, intentional cause
This ticket is caused by an invalid account
questions.explain: Because Transfer to GL had already run twice successfully with no errors, the cause here could not be a simple timing gap — it required looking at a different mechanism (the Transfer to GL attribute).

questions.q: What does the 'Transfer to GL' accounting attribute set to N actually do?
options: It tells Subledger Accounting to intentionally exclude that entry from any transfer run, regardless of how many times the transfer program runs
Nothing — it has no functional effect
It automatically reverses the journal entry
It forces the entry into a suspense account
questions.explain: When set to N, this per-entry attribute deliberately excludes the accounted entry from being transferred to GL, by design rather than by error.

questions.q: Why was the Transfer to GL attribute set to N for this Receivables adjustment type in the first place?
options: It was a random system default
It was caused by a recent patch
A clerk accidentally changed it on one entry
It was deliberately set that way months ago to support an internal reporting process that has since been discontinued, and was never reverted
questions.explain: The setting was intentional at the time, tied to a now-discontinued reporting process, but nobody reverted it after that process ended.

questions.q: What is the correct resolution, given that the setting was deliberate at the time it was configured?
options: Leave the setting as is since it was originally intentional
Confirm with the SLA setup owner that nothing still depends on the old behavior, then update the attribute so these entries transfer going forward
Delete the adjustment type entirely
Force a manual journal entry into GL instead of transferring
questions.explain: Since the original business reason no longer applies, the fix is to confirm it's safe and then update the setting so future entries of this type transfer normally.

questions.q: Why does the resolution note recommend a periodic review of 'exclude from transfer' settings tied to discontinued processes?
options: Because Oracle automatically removes such settings after a set time
Because it is required for SOX compliance in all cases
Because this type of setting has no natural expiration and can silently persist long after its original business reason is gone
Because it only applies to Receivables
questions.explain: Unlike a timing gap that resolves itself, a deliberate setting like this stays in place indefinitely unless someone proactively reviews and reverts it.
